self_corrections: Sign bug: picks['exploit'] used argsort(-p), which selects the LARGEST predicted viability (the worst regimens). The same sign error affected contender and exploit_instab. First-run results renamed *_INVALID_SIGNS* and not cited.

VOI and exploit are analytically identical under a homoscedastic Gaussian prior: P(u is best) is a strictly decreasing function of p_u, so ranking by it equals ranking by p. Three arms agree to 0.0000 in the corrected run. E009 therefore does NOT test decision-theoretic active learning.

Replace-by-measurement is not a Bayesian update: swapping a multi-cell prior (sigma ~ 0.13/sqrt(13)) for a single-cell measurement (sigma ~ 0.03-0.04) lowers precision, which explains the k=1,2 penalty. Not evidence that acquisition is useless.

result.verdict: no acquisition strategy beats not buying / exploitation under this implementation
